correctness.rationale: For the published radial function, direct differentiation yields a curvature numerator equal to 1+epsilon(2c-c^3) after removal of a strictly positive denominator. Exact one-variable calculus shows that 2c-c^3 has the unique minimum -4*sqrt(6)/9 at c=-sqrt(2/3). Thus the meridian has nonnegative curvature exactly through epsilon=3*sqrt(6)/8, strictly positive curvature below it, and negative curvature above it. The endpoint is convex by Hausdorff closure of convex compact sets. The bundled checker independently reconstructs the factorization and exact extremum.
